text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The exchange rate of the leu might stabilise at around 7,000-7,500 against the dollar in the near future, the paper quotes central bank governor Mugur Isarescu as saying.
- The government plans to "borrow" some 200,000 tonnes of wheat, to meet local demand until the new wheat crop is harvested in July, the paper says.
- Some 7.0 percent of Romania's population live under the poverty threshold, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The government plans cuts in customs taxes for imports of food products, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The World Bank will give Romania loans worth $500 million to support reforms in the farming sector.
- Italy's Fiat might sign cooperation accord with Tractorul Brasov tractor maker, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The opposition National Unity Party (PUNR) sacked its nationalist leader Gheorghe Funar and elected ex-farm minister Valeriu Tabara as the new head of PUNR.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania has 106 cases of tuberculosis per 100,000 inhabitants, the highest rate in Europe.
- The six Taiwanese sailors charged with casting three Romanian stowaways overboard to perish on the high sea were released on bail, the paper says.
- Bucharest homeless seek shelter in the crypts of Bellu cemetery.
ADEVARUL
- Prosecutors accused coal miners' leader Miron Cosma of allegedly undermining the state authority and breaking firearms regulations during a 1991 miners' riot in Bucharest.
- Romania's chances to join NATO remained unaltered after the Helsinki summit, the newspaper says in editorial.
- The Hungarian Democratic Union wants bilingual signs to be used in localities where ethnic Hungarians represent more than 10 percent of the population.
- Romania's king Michael I, on a visit to Britain to seek support for Romania's early NATO admission, is expected to meet Prince Charles and have a private lunch with Queen Elisabeth.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Turkish Interior Minister Meral Aksener starts two-day visit to Bucharest.
- The opposition Party of Social Democracy set up a hotline for what it called victims of political cleansing. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
